data_flow.step: A fact-check execution finishes. On a FAIL (any verdict other than Pass), consecutive_fails is incremented, pending_findings is set to the findings text, and needs_run is set. A PASS sets consecutive_fails to 0.

next_steps runs spec_flow or plan_flow. If a recurring gate is already open (recurring_gate is Some) the flow returns early. Otherwise, when the author needs a rerun, pending_findings is Some and consecutive_fails >= FACTCHECK_RECURRING_LIMIT + fail_limit_extra, the planner calls self.gate(title, explanation, GatePayload::FactCheckRecurring {...}) instead of spawning the author.

Planner::gate pushes Step::OpenGate { title, explanation, payload }. The runner turns it into a gate-opened event; the fold stores the gate id in spec.recurring_gate or plan.recurring_gate by target (state.rs lines 3857-3859). gate_owner returns the target string as the dedupe key part.

On answer, the fold clears the recurring gate; 'stop' sets stopped (the next planner pass emits Step::Fail 'The spec stage was stopped.' or 'The plan stage was stopped.'); any other choice calls allow_more, and optional guidance text becomes a spec change (spec.changes + needs_run) or goes through requirement_change for the plan, via the Route-answer judge when routed.
Under YOLO the gate is answered by a fixed plan: another-round while passes < 6, else stop.

patterns.description: In spec_flow, inside the branch that runs when the spec has no current version or needs a rerun, the planner checks that findings are pending and that consecutive_fails has reached the limit plus the extension. It then opens the gate with the findings of the current check and returns false, so no spawn happens. The spec explanation has an extra sentence ('Another round may not converge.') that the plan explanation lacks.
patterns.name: Spec gate open site

patterns.description: In plan_flow, same condition with an extra !t.invalidated guard (a plan invalidated by a spec change reruns without the gate and without findings). Title and explanation are plan-specific; the explanation omits the 'may not converge' sentence.
patterns.name: Plan gate open site

patterns.description: The limit is a constant of 3, but the compared threshold is 3 + fail_limit_extra. Answering anything other than stop calls allow_more, which sets fail_limit_extra to the current consecutive_fails. The next gate therefore opens after three further FAILs (6, 9, ...), as the docs say. Only a PASS resets consecutive_fails to 0 and the extension is not reset with it (fact_finished sets consecutive_fails = 0 on PASS and leaves fail_limit_extra alone).
patterns.name: Limit extension on another-round

document.problem: The planner opens a FactCheckRecurring gate from two separate places, one in spec_flow and one in plan_flow, each with its own title and explanation string. Both compare the track's consecutive FAIL count against FACTCHECK_RECURRING_LIMIT plus a per-track extension. The two explanation strings differ in wording.

submit.findings_summary: The planner opens the gate in crates/ostra-engine/src/plan.rs: spec_flow (lines 798-815) and plan_flow (lines 969-984), through Planner::gate(title, explanation, payload). Both open it when pending_findings is Some and consecutive_fails >= FACTCHECK_RECURRING_LIMIT (3, defined in state.rs:35) + fail_limit_extra. plan_flow also requires !t.invalidated. The spec explanation is "The fact-check has failed {n} times in a row. Another round may not converge. Choose whether to run another round, add guidance, or stop." The plan explanation is the same without the "may not converge" sentence. Titles are "The spec fact-check keeps failing" and "The plan fact-check keeps failing". Answering another-round sets fail_limit_extra = consecutive_fails (state.rs:4818), so the next gate opens three FAILs later. YOLO answers another-round while passes < 6 using a literal 6 in judge_input.rs:1009. The docs in docs/internals/gates-and-judges.md and pipeline.md repeat the limit.
